claims.text: The starting material is eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high-entropy alloy in the as-cast condition.
The as-cast alloy has a hierarchical microstructure consisting of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The starting alloy has relatively coarse lamellar spacing.
Coarse lamellar boundaries promote large dislocation pile-ups in the as-cast alloy.
Large dislocation pile-ups at coarse lamellar boundaries are a primary cause of the starting alloy's limited ductility and brittleness.
Cold rolling to approximately 70–80% reduction followed by annealing near 650 °C for 30–60 minutes will refine the lamellar colonies and decrease inter-phase spacing.
The proposed processing will produce refined, uniformly distributed lamellar colonies.
Reduced lamellar spacing limits the dislocation mean free path.
Limiting the dislocation mean free path reduces the size and intensity of dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries.
Smaller dislocation pile-ups produce a more homogeneous distribution of local stresses during deformation.
The refined structure enhances work hardening.
More homogeneous local stresses and enhanced work hardening delay the onset of microcracking and brittle failure.
The treatment will increase room-temperature tensile ductility by more than 50% relative to the as-cast state.
The treatment will prevent any decrease in yield strength and may increase yield strength relative to the as-cast state.
The predicted improvement applies under room-temperature, quasi-static loading conditions.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration can coarsen the microstructure and reduce the treatment's benefits.
